note.text: Browser pane dialogs: only a beforeunload ("Leave site?") dialog is answered for an agent (Leave, when the tab's agent acted within LEAVE_AFTER_CALL, 5 s). Alert and confirm are left to the user on purpose, not merely not done yet: clicking OK on a confirm by itself could approve something like a delete. They can still stall an agent the same way, so handling them needs a decision, not just code.

Browser pane: every tab runs Page.enable and listens for Page.javascriptDialogOpening. A beforeunload ("Leave site?") dialog opening within LEAVE_AFTER_CALL (5 s) of the tab's agent call (Tab.called, set by devtools calls, web::navigate and go_in with an id) is answered Leave via Page.handleJavaScriptDialog. Default dialogs stay enabled, so the user's own dialogs still show. Other dialog kinds (alert, confirm) are not handled yet.

A dev instance leaves the quest log of every project the installed Horadric knows to the installed one: its runner skips those boards (App::dev_leaves_to_installed, runner.rs dev_leaves), reading the installed state.json's `recent` list from %APPDATA%\Horadric at most every 30 s. Set HORADRIC_DEV_QUESTS=1 to test the runner itself, or use a folder only the dev instance knows. Why: on 2026-10-16 a dev instance started to try a build (even target\release\horadric.exe during a ship public) took the real horadric.dev quest "Memory: no recall on a task notification" in its own hosts, then the dev instance and its hosts were stopped and the quest sat [/] with nobody on it for 14 hours. CLAUDE.md says Warriv skips them too; only the runner's side was checked in code here.

A dev instance started to try a build (HORADRIC_DEV=1, even target\release\horadric.exe during a ship public) runs its quest runner on the real horadric.dev quest log and starts real quest sessions in its own hosts. On 2026-10-16 it took "Memory: no recall on a task notification" (session f2853656, its prompt said to run target/release/horadric.exe quest done), then the dev instance and its hosts were stopped and the quest sat [/] with nobody on it for 14 hours. Its state is in %APPDATA%\Horadric-dev\state.json.

Fixed 2026-11-01: the wake at work is kept per project in state.json as `Heard::awake` (a `warriv::Kept`, with given events, settled, told, filed, aims). `State::after` adopts it as `Awake::after` (told_at at the epoch, `adopted` true), and `State::heard` writes it. An adopted wake's turn counts as over when its session is Idle (`warriv::turn_over`), because after a reload `attach_hosts` sets Idle for a session between turns and its Stop went unheard. `App::freeze` cuts wakes short only on a quit that ends the sessions (`quit && stop_on_exit`), before the final save. After a crash the kept wake has no host: `drop_lost_wakes` closes its tile and `orchestrate` retires it, handing what it left unsettled to the human. The double "slept" line at a reload is gone with this.

Trap, not fixed: `Camp::awake` lives only in memory (`State::after` restores just the desk's heard events), and `App::cut_wakes_short` records every awake wake as slept at a reload too. So after a reload a wake that was mid-turn keeps running in its host but no camp tracks it: its end is never handled, its tile stays after its turn, and the next event starts a second wake beside it. Fixing it means keeping the awake id in state.json and adopting it in `State::after`.

Keeper restart while the owner is dead (fixed 078064e, was #495's first gap): keeping_restore runs once at the first keeping_tick and calls far_restore (far.rs) for each brother with stores, inserting a Peer with via None and Heard from restored_heard (newest of holding.seen.heard and snapshot mtime, last said). Tiles come from kept_entry. Holding.seen (heard, said, name, project, phase) is the keeper's own word, written by keeping_note at most every 60s of new hearing (seen_due) under RECEIVING.try_lock, and carried over when a new snapshot rewrites holding.json. keeping_turn_for now also requires waited(last, started, now): an owner not heard since this run began gets SILENT_SECS from the start before offer, click or auto takeover. keeping_prune only marks a tile 'seen' while its brother is ready, so a restored tile never counts as the owner listing it. Live test recipe in scratchpad rs/ of session ecc27607 (start.ps1, rclick.ps1 posts tile clicks, tray.ps1).

Keeper gap (found 2026-10-24, not fixed): a keeper offers "Take over" (tile menu and the phone's "take" list) only for a brother tile it already shows and a brother it heard this run. If the keeper restarts while the owner is dead, it has no tile for the owner's sessions and far_presence is None, so nothing can be taken over until the owner comes back, though the snapshots sit on disk under keeping/<brother id>/. handing_takeable and keeping_offer both start from registry brother tiles. Also: a session handed to a PC lands in a linked worktree that goes into that PC's recent list first; handing::land now finds the main tree from it (worktree::main_top, commit 31494bf), before that the next handoff or takeover into the project failed with "not a main working tree".

Lore marks are line ending independent since c4d3f66: a note's file hash (`Mark`, taken by `Place::hash` in horadric-hooks) and each symbol's `Piece::hash` are `lore::text_hash`, FNV-1a with every CRLF read as LF, so a note shared between a CRLF Windows checkout (core.autocrlf) and an LF Linux node stays fresh on both. Old notes held FNV of the raw bytes: `lore::unchanged` (used by `parts::Tree`'s `Now::same`) and `part_changed` (via `Piece::raw`) accept that hash too, so they stay fresh on the machine that took them; a CRLF-era note seen on the LF brother is still maybe stale until retaken. `Now::same` defaults to plain equality for trees without bytes (`recall::hashes`). The code index's store key (`code::key`) still hashes raw bytes, which is fine because code chunks match through `Tree::same`.

Open: a shared note that names a file shows MAYBE STALE on the other brother when one checkout has CRLF and the other LF (Git for Windows with core.autocrlf=true). Seen in step 16's test: a note left on Windows naming README.md was stale on the Linux node though the commit was the same. The marks hash the file's bytes as checked out, so line endings count; hashing the git blob, or normalising line endings, would fix it.

`horadric heavy` now has N slots: slot i is a file lock in %TEMP%\horadric-heavy (slot 0 keeps the old names slot.lock/slot.json so older builds still queue with it; others slot-1.lock/slot-1.json), from `heavy::slots`: HORADRIC_HEAVY_SLOTS if it parses, else one per 16 logical cores, clamped 1 to 8. With one slot a waiter blocks on the lock (keeps waiters in turn); with more it polls every 500 ms. While waiting, a thread in `take` posts a `Queued` to /horadric/heavy (command header "heavy") every 15 s and waiting:false when done; the app turns it into `HookEvent::HEAVY`, which `Session::apply` stores in `heavy` without touching heard_at or the phase. `Session::queued_line` shows "queued for heavy behind ..." on the tile only while Working and within 45 s of the last post, since a killed waiter never says it stopped. Not shown for sessions on a Linux node (the field is not serialized over the wire).

`horadric heavy -- <command>` runs a test suite or full build only while no other session on the machine runs one (sessions sharing the CPU all finish late). The slot is a file lock, %TEMP%\horadric-heavy\slot.lock (holder in slot.json), which the OS frees however its holder ends, so a killed session holds nobody up; dev and installed Horadric share it. A waiter is told whose command it waits for; `horadric heavy` alone says who holds it. Never wrap a dev server or watcher in it. Not built: the tile does not show a session waiting for the slot, and there is always exactly one slot.

Cross building the Linux node on Windows now needs a C compiler, since `ring` (in horadric-link) and the memory's C are compiled for the target. What works on this PC: zig 0.17 from `winget install zig.zig` (lives in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WinGet\Packages\zig.zig_*\zig-x86_64-windows-0.17.0, put it on PATH) and `cargo install cargo-zigbuild`, then `cargo zigbuild --release -p horadric --bin horadric --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` (or `-p horadric-link --tests`), with a separate CARGO_TARGET_DIR to avoid lock fights. zig both compiles the C and links, so no rust-lld setting is needed. The result is a static ELF; a musl test binary copied to exit1-eu with C:/Windows/System32/OpenSSH/scp.exe (gzip it first, debug is 76 MB) runs there as `agent`. WSL is not installed. CI and release-linux.yml use gcc and musl-tools instead.

The Linux node binary cross builds on Windows with no musl toolchain: `rustup target add x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`, then `CARGO_TARGET_X86_64_UNKNOWN_LINUX_MUSL_LINKER=rust-lld cargo build --release -p horadric --bin horadric --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` (a separate CARGO_TARGET_DIR avoids lock fights). It comes out static-pie and ran on the exit1-eu VPS. Copy with C:/Windows/System32/OpenSSH/scp.exe to ~/.local/bin/horadric, then `horadric node install` there. On exit1-eu as agent the node listens on 127.0.0.1:43117 (not 43118), and `loginctl enable-linger agent` succeeded without root.

Memory embedding pace (since e683a88, 2026-10-30): embedding runs on its own pool of two threads below normal priority (horadric-memory lib.rs), not rayon's global pool of a thread per core, which kept a core or more busy beside six working sessions; Whisper keeps the global pool. The background still embeds `STEP` 2 chunks then rests `REST` 100 ms while nothing is asked; a recall first embeds the asking project's new notes for at most `UNASKED_BUDGET` and friends. Code is synced at most every `SYNC_EVERY` 30 s. The memory thread now lives in crates/horadric-memory/src/service.rs (re-exported as `horadric_ui::memory`, shared with the Linux node), not horadric-ui/src/memory.rs.

Memory thread pacing (horadric-ui memory.rs): a recall first embeds the asking project's new notes, newest first, for at most 3 s (1 s for a prompt recall, 0.5 s for a quest's unasked recall); everything else is embedded in the background STEP 2 chunks at a time with a 100 ms REST while nothing is asked. The model uses every core while it runs. Fine for notes, but the backlog of transcript chunks will want a gentler pace (not done). Code is synced at most every 30 s.

Context pack tuned 2026-11-01 with `horadric quest spend`: 52 packed quests, median 3.6M tokens and 37 calls of 99k, against 73 without at 6.4M and 55 calls of 108k (confounded: lore notes, code index and the subagent prompt came in the same weeks). New lines `pack::uptake` (packs given) and `pack::replay` (the current drawing replayed over every done quest from the quests done before it). Given packs: 49, 37% of their files used (places 1 to 4 50%, 5 to 8 32%, 9 to 12 28%), naming 25% of what quests touched. Replay grid over 117 packs: LIKE 5 beat 3 on precision and recall at every size (12 files: 35%/29% vs 34%/27%), so `LIKE` is 5. MOST stays 12: 8 files gives 42%/23%, a hint line costs a few tokens while even places 9 to 12 are used about a quarter of the time. The change weight stays 2.0 (1.0 and 4.0 no better). `pack_with` and `Tuning` let a tuning be tried.

Context pack measured with `horadric quest spend`: baseline 2026-10-15, 63 quests without a pack, median 6.5M tokens and 60 calls, Read 8%. On 2026-10-16 with 10 packed quests: median 4.9M and 45 calls (Read 6%) against 6.3M and 55 without (73 quests): about 22% fewer tokens and 18% fewer calls, from less searching rather than less reading. Small sample, and the lore's notes and code index arrived at the same time, so the pack does not own the whole drop. The pack stays on; rerun quest spend past 30 packed quests before tuning its size or weights (not done yet).

Headless Claude protocol, confirmed on Claude Code 2.1.312 (2026-10-29), replacing #504's guesses. Start claude.exe with --input-format=stream-json --output-format=stream-json --verbose --include-partial-messages --permission-prompt-tool=stdio. No -p and no initialize request needed; can_use_tool comes over stdio without it. With CLAUDECODE, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN stripped, init says apiKeySource "none". Prompt: {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":TEXT},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":""}, not echoed back. system/init repeats at the start of every turn. init's permissionMode follows the user's settings ("auto" never asks): pass --permission-mode=default to get asks. can_use_tool request has tool_name, input, description, permission_suggestions; allow echoes updatedInput, a deny returns as a tool_result with is_error true. Each content block streams (start, deltas, stop) and its whole copy also comes as an assistant message, one block per message, same message id, usually just before content_block_stop: dedupe by message id. Thinking streams empty. A tool_result can arrive while the next tool_use still streams. Interrupt control_request gets control_response {"still_queued":[]}, then the cut-short assistant text, a user text "[Request interrupted by user]", and a result with is_error true, subtype error_during_execution, terminal_reason aborted_streaming; the process takes the next prompt. Hooks fire: SessionStart hook_started and hook_response show as system lines. Also seen: system status, system thinking_tokens, rate_limit_event.

Headless Claude protocol (researched 2026-10-24, CLI 2.1.310, for docs/plan/headless.md). Start claude.exe, never claude.cmd: --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose, plus --include-partial-messages and --permission-prompt-tool stdio; values in --resume=<id> form. The SDK passes no -p (unconfirmed if needed). Strip CLAUDECODE, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN so the subscription login is used (init apiKeySource "none"); --bare never uses OAuth. Stdin NDJSON user: {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":...},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"default"}, optional uuid, priority now|next|later, client_composed. Control: {"type":"control_request","request_id":..,"request":{"subtype":initialize|interrupt|set_permission_mode|set_model|get_context_usage|rewind_files}}. Answer CLI requests with {"type":"control_response","response":{"subtype":"success","request_id":..,"response":..}}; can_use_tool allow {"behavior":"allow","updatedInput":<echo input>} or deny {"behavior":"deny","message":..}. AskUserQuestion is a can_use_tool: allow with updatedInput {questions, answers:{question:label}}. ExitPlanMode probably the same. Stdout: system/init (session_id, slash_commands, skills, capabilities), assistant blocks (parent_tool_use_id marks subagents), user tool_result, stream_event deltas, one result per turn (is_error may be true with subtype success; terminal_reason aborted_* after interrupt), conversation_reset after /clear. Slash commands are plain text. Keep stdin open; read stdout on its own thread; lines can pass 1 MB. The control protocol is undocumented (from claude-agent-sdk-python _internal/query.py) and may change: detect features by capabilities. Docs: code.claude.com/docs/en/headless.md, agent-sdk/user-input.md, authentication.md.

Coming back to Horadric opens at most one thing. The catch-up (catchup::Away, tested) counts as away after 15 minutes without input (GetLastInputInfo, polled every second, catchup.rs AWAY_AFTER) or with the screen locked (WTSRegisterSessionNotification); input within 5 s or unlocking is coming back, input on the lock screen is not. It opens only if something happened, and not while Windows asks for quiet, as toasts. The away card (built 2026-10-05, away.rs AWAY_FOR) takes its place after 30 minutes away with news in any quest log, so coming back is one card. A question asked before the human left is shown again but opens nothing. The card stands over the stage, at most 520 DIPs wide, and does not close on losing focus, since answering often means reading a session first. An answer is the human's, not Warriv's: the session is told "The human answers: ...", or a gone session's quest gets a `The human answers:` note and starts again. The catch-up opens on demand from the tray and the "Stay a while and listen" shortcut (hotkey.rs, Ctrl+Alt+Home by default, Shift added on a dev instance, changeable in Settings): since local midnight, or the last eight hours early in the day, and it says "Nothing happened" rather than staying shut. Windows may refuse focus to an app you are not using, so then it closes when focus moves anywhere. On a dev instance a file `away-now` in the state folder fakes coming back from an hour away. Not tried on screen: coming back after 15 minutes or an unlock, clicking a line, the tray item, an answer typed into a live session between turns.

The away card (built 2026-10-05): after 30 minutes with no input (`GetLastInputInfo`) and news in any quest log, one card opens on return and takes the catch-up's place, so coming back is one card; shorter or no news, the catch-up opens as before. A question asked before the human left is shown again but opens nothing. It stands over the stage, at most 520 DIPs wide, and does not close on losing focus, since answering often means reading a session first. An answer is the human's, not Warriv's: the session is told "The human answers: ...", or a gone session's quest gets a `The human answers:` note and starts again. On a dev instance, a file `away-now` in the state folder fakes coming back from an hour away. Not tried on screen: an answer typed into a live session between turns.

One portal, PC side (built 2026-11-01): `Portal::pair` in portaling.rs pairs v3 when the phone's `pair` has v>=3 and `key` AND this PC has a key pair (`Signer::of`); else it pairs v2. v3 stores the DERIVED key as `Phone.key` in portal.json with `Phone.public` beside it, so `portal::identify` works unchanged; an upgraded v2 phone keeps its old key in `Phone.was`, which identify also tries. `Portal::look_at_word` (every 2 s from `portal_check`) recomputes `served` (phones the signed word serves, keys derived via `phoning::Keys`, which caches each ECDH) and drops a config phone whose public key a held `forgets` names. `unpair_forgotten` keeps a channel only if its phone is in config OR served. `upgrade` and `forget` messages are taken in `heard_from` before the Server; `brothers` is sent by `App::portal_tell_brothers` after each drain, per channel only when its fingerprint changed (`Portal::told`, cleared at hello).

One portal, state on 2026-10-31: the words are built (`What::Vouches`, `What::Forgets`, `said::phones`, `mesh::vouch`, `mesh::forget`) but only the simulations call `mesh::vouch` and `mesh::forget`. The PC still pairs phones the v2 way (`portaling.rs` answers `{"t":"paired","phone","key"}` with a symmetric key; `far_phone.rs` sends `"v":2`), so no phone is vouched for in the signed word yet and the label "horadric phone key v1" exists only in the page. The page side (`../horadric.portal/public/phonekey.js`, its framing mirrors `joining::derive`, and v3 pairing and the upgrade offer in `app.js`) was written but not committed as of this date. Note: the "v3" in `portal.rs` and `serving.rs` is the older raw stream protocol, not pairing v3. What is left is in docs/plan/one-portal.md.
